title: Pruning already chosen elements in permutations
summary: Along the choice path 1 → 3 → 2, use selected to prune element indices already used in the current permutation prefix.
context: The input is choices = [1, 2, 3] (indices 0, 1, 2), with distinct elements, and each element may be used at most once in a permutation. Here state holds the current permutation prefix, while the Boolean array selected tracks by input index whether each element has already been chosen on the current path.
description: The selected array only prevents reusing an index along the current recursive path: descending skips marked indices, and backtracking unmarks them on return, so choosing 1 does not disable 1 permanently—it remains available in other permutation branches.

The figure fully expands only the path [] → [1] → [1, 3] → [1, 3, 2]. Pruning marks denote repeated selections that are not entered, such as [1, 1] for choosing element 1 at index 0 again under prefix [1]; ellipses mark valid branches whose continuations are left unexpanded.
